Below are top options prioritized by funding level. When reviewing university scholarships connected to University of Amsterdam, these are often the first awards worth checking due to the typical scale of support. Amsterdam Merit Scholarships for Master’s Students is usually considered fully funded, and typical coverage can include full tuition fees and an additional allowance of €5,000 for students in the Graduate School of Business and Economics, A cash award of €25,900 for students in the Law School, and A cash award of €15,000 for students in the Graduate School of Science. A strong option is Amsterdam Economics and Business Talent Fund which is fully funded and often covers full tuition fee waiver for one year and study costs for one year. Amsterdam Merit Scholarship for Undergraduate Students is partially funded, and coverage often includes A cash award of various amount per year for students in Economics, business, social and behavioral sciences, and Psychology programs (amount is determined each year and varies). If you are building a wider scholarship strategy for University of Amsterdam, external and government programs can be important additions. Here are a few to consider. Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions is fully funded and typically covers living stipend, mobility allowance, and special needs, leave, and and/or family allowance (if applicable). Apply now University of Amsterdam FAQ Are there any scholarships at the University of Amsterdam that are for online courses? There are no online scholarships for online programs for regular degrees at University of Amsterdam. For which subjects does the University of Amsterdam offer scholarships for? At the master’s level, there are Child Development and Education, Communication Science, Economics and Business, Humanities, Law, Medicine, Psychology, Science, and Social Sciences. At bachelor’s level, the coverage is narrower, especially Economics and Business, Social and Behavioural Sciences, and Psychology, with Economics and Business scholarships specifically mentioning areas such as Business Administration, Economics and Business Economics, Actuarial Science, Business Analytics, and Econometrics and Data Science. So business, humanities, law, medicine, and STEM are all represented. For engineering, UvA is better described as offering engineering-related fields such as Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Security and Network Engineering, and Software Engineering and Green IT rather than a broad classical engineering faculty. For which nationalities does the University of Amsterdam offer scholarships for? The main UvA-wide answer is that the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship is primarily for non-EU/EEA students at both bachelor’s and master’s level. That matches the UvA stories here: winners came from Kazakhstan, Brazil, and Ecuador. Is having a language proficiency test necessary (IELTS, TOEFL) for the University of Amsterdam? Often yes, but not always. At bachelor’s level, UvA generally requires proof of English at C1 level unless you qualify for an exemption through your prior education, with common minimums such as IELTS 6.5 overall or TOEFL iBT 92. At master’s level, the exact test and score depend on the faculty or programme, but IELTS/TOEFL are commonly required unless you qualify for an exemption. This matches the recipient stories. According to Melina Coelho Garcia , “To study at the UvA, I had to take the IELTS.” Banu Keikina also said she had to retake IELTS before applying for her master’s because her earlier result had expired. Is there a minimum grade for acceptance at the University of Amsterdam? There is no single university-wide minimum grade that covers every programme. For bachelor’s admission, UvA checks your country-specific or diploma-specific eligibility. For master’s admission, some programmes publish minimum GPA thresholds, while competitive scholarships usually expect much more. For example, UvA’s Master’s in Artificial Intelligence lists a minimum equivalent of 6.5 Dutch / 3.0 US / 2.1 UK, Business Administration asks for an average GPA of 7.0 or higher, and some scholarship pages mention very high benchmarks such as 3.7 or even 4.0 equivalents. The recipients were clearly strong applicants: Banu Keikina had a 4.16/4.30 GPA, Melina Coelho Garcia had 9.7/10, and Belén Estrella Fiallo reported 92/100 in her bachelor’s plus 18.9/20 in the IB. Is there an age limit to get scholarships at the University of Amsterdam? There’s no official university-wide age limit on the UvA scholarships. The published criteria focus on nationality, admission status, grades, motivation, financial situation, documents, and visa compliance, and age is not a standard published requirements. What is a good academic background and the minimum eligibility to get a scholarship at the University of Amsterdam? A good academic background for UvA scholarships usually means a relevant prior diploma or degree, strong grades, a clear fit with the programme, proof of English if required, and a complete application. For the main Amsterdam Merit Scholarship, the standard starting point is usually non-EU/EEA status plus an application to a UvA degree programme, while faculty-level scholarships may additionally ask for recommendation letters, a motivation letter, or proof of financial need. The recipient stories make this more concrete: Banu Keikina paired a 4.16/4.30 GPA with seven internships; Melina Coelho Garcia combined a 9.7/10 law GPA with research, moot competitions, and NGO work; and Belén Estrella Fiallo described strong grades plus student groups, creative work, and a professional portfolio.
